sources.claim: National-framework reporting (Washington Blade, 10 Apr 2025): President Milei eliminated the federal Women, Gender and Diversity Ministry, dismissed trans employees hired under the Trans Labour Quota Law (which reserved at least 1% of public-sector jobs for trans people), and on 5 Feb 2025 issued a decree restricting minors' access to gender-affirming surgery and hormone treatments. Argentine trans activists interviewed 4 Apr 2025 describe the community as facing a 'chaotic, desperate' situation with heightened exposure to violence, discrimination and poverty; the 2012 Gender Identity Law (legal gender change without medical gatekeeping) remains on the books. This national framework is what a trans visitor stands under in this Argentine province.

National-framework report (Agencia Presentes, 19 Mar 2026) on the Observatorio Nacional de Crimenes de Odio LGBT+ figures: 2025 set a record with at least 227 bias-motivated crimes against LGBT people in Argentina (up on 2024), one every 38 hours; 62.5% of victims (142) were trans women or travestis, 18 trans men (vs 5 in 2024), 13 lesbians and 4 non-binary people; 64.8% (147 cases) were physical violence and 32% occurred in police stations or penal institutions, with police involvement jumping from 17 cases in 2024 to 64 in 2025. Frame applies to this province as part of the national position.

records.name: Tucumán
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. The national frame is what matters here: the 2025 hate-crime record (227 murders, +62% on 2024, most perpetrators police or public-space strangers) and the February 2025 presidential decrees cutting the Gender Identity Law apply in Tucumán as elsewhere, while the province carries neither the metros' trans sex-work policing nor a documented community presence - and the dossier cautions that at these numbers a single provincial case is a real signal, so a zero should not be read as safety.

records.name: Lower Silesian Voivodeship
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. The voivodeship's municipalities recur in the national court history annulling anti-LGBT declarations - annulments the Supreme Administrative Court upheld in May 2022 and on 28 June 2022, holding the resolutions violate the dignity of LGBT people and risk violence - a pattern running in the protective direction across all of Poland.

sources.claim: Case report (Association for Legal Intervention, 13 Mar 2024): a Polish regional court placed a transgender Vietnamese woman who had been on hormone therapy since 2018 in a guarded centre for male foreigners, and the Border Guard refused to move or release her despite Polish law barring placement wherever a stay would threaten life or health or the person shows signs of having suffered violence. After the association's application to the Border Guard Post commander she was released (page updated 28 Mar 2024). Establishes the current framework for trans foreigners in Polish immigration detention - directly relevant to any trans visitor detained while in this voivodeship.

ECtHR ruling coverage (TGEU, 16 Jul 2024): on 11 Jul 2024 the European Court of Human Rights found Polish prison authorities violated a trans woman's right to private and family life (Article 8 ECHR) by denying her hormone-replacement therapy in Siedlce prison, awarding EUR 8,000 damages; the Court left the alleged Articles 3 and 14 breaches undecided but held the refusal had no reasonable legal grounds and was disproportionate. The judgment is binding on Poland as a whole - the governing standard for trans people's healthcare in Polish prisons and detention in every voivodeship, including this one.
